prompt: Analyze the provided character sheet for sprite extraction and alignment. Return ONLY valid JSON with no Markdown or extra text. Detect every distinct character in reading order (top-to-bottom, left-to-right). Do not assume a fixed grid, equal spacing, shared width or height, or a repeated coordinate template. Use pixel coordinates with origin at the image top-left. For each character independently, trace the outermost visible foreground pixels on all four sides. Include every visible pixel belonging to that character, including hair, hands, feet, clothing, held weapons, equipment, accessories, and antialiased edge pixels. Exclude background, shadows, and neighboring characters. After finding the observed outermost foreground pixels, expand the bbox by 3 pixels on every side, clipped to the image bounds and without including a neighbor. Different silhouettes should normally produce different bbox coordinates and dimensions. Before returning, verify for every item that no visible foreground pixel belonging to it lies outside its bbox. Define foot_anchor as the two-dimensional center of the lowest visible sole contact span belonging to the character; exclude weapons, hanging accessories, shadows, and unrelated objects from this anchor. If both feet touch the ground, use the center spanning both sole contacts. If only one foot touches, use that sole center. Return exactly this structure: {"image_width":integer,"image_height":integer,"items":[{"index":integer,"bbox":{"x":integer,"y":integer,"width":integer,"height":integer},"foot_anchor":{"x":number,"y":number}}]}. CRITICAL: foot_anchor MUST always be a JSON object containing both x and y. Never return foot_anchor as a single number, array, string, null, or any other shape. Correct example: "foot_anchor":{"x":177.5,"y":340}. Assign zero-based index values in reading order. bbox width and height must be positive. Every JSON property name, including x and y, must be enclosed in double quotes. Before returning, verify every item has exactly one numeric foot_anchor.x and one numeric foot_anchor.y. Do not invent obscured boundaries or coordinates.
